caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000003
attempts.paper_title: Physiological Properties and Behavioral Correlates of Hippocampal Granule Cells and Mossy Cells
attempts.entry_title: Granule cells and mossy cells of the dentate gyrus (Senzai and Buzsaki 2017)
attempts.summary: Most main findings hold up: granule and mossy cells separate as described, mossy cells fire more, and granule cells fire most in NREM sleep, lock more strongly to theta and gamma, excite mossy cells with burst facilitation and carry less spatial information. Two did not reproduce: weaker granule-to-mossy transmission in NREM sleep, which depends on the authors' manual curation of pairs, and less open-field remapping in granule than mossy cells (P = 0.69). Optogenetic tagging matched the paper only under a per-bin reading of the suppression rule. Some smaller claims, such as CA3 cells firing most in wake, did not hold. The distance between connected cells and dendritic backpropagation were untested, as the claims file gives no criterion.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Senzai and Buzsaki (2017) on dandiset 000003, silicon probe recordings from the dentate gyrus and CA3 of 15 of the paper's mice. It compares granule cells, mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells by the authors' labels, their waveforms, rates by brain state, theta and gamma phase locking, firing around dentate spikes, optogenetic suppression in DRD2-Cre mice, monosynaptic and zero-lag pairs from cross-correlograms, place fields on the circular T-maze and remapping between open fields, and repeats the paper's k-means separation of granule and mossy cells on the files that hold the wide-band signal.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Senzai and Buzsaki (2017) from dandiset 000003
The findings of senzai-2017-01, checked on version 0.261122.2143

outcomes.statement: The second-stage classification divided dentate excitatory neurons into 586 putative granule cells (GC) and 500 putative mossy cells (MC).
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 2; Figure 1F
outcomes.quote: K-means clustering on the three sets of features reliably segregated excitatory neurons as putative granule cells (n = 586) and putative mossy cells (n = 500)
outcomes.notes: The cell_type labels give 583 granule cells and 503 mossy cells in the 15 mice of the paper, each with its own global_id (no repeats), within 10% of 586 and 500. With YutaMouse57, which is not in the paper, the labels give 609 and 568. Whether the two files of a day hold the same neurons is not settled. In YutaMouse51 on 16 May, 0.56 of the 9 GC, MC or CA3 units of the 'b' file have a same-type unit on the same shank in the other file of the day with a waveform correlation above 0.95, against none of 9 on another day. In the other six pairs at most 0.38 exceed 0.95, and in two of them a file of another day matches as often or more often (YutaMouse54 'b' 1 July 0.18 against 0.29; YutaMouse55 'b' 7 September 0.38 and 0.38).
deviations: The labels are the authors' (the files' cell_type, from their unit summary); the second-stage k-means is repeated separately under gc-mc-classification.

outcomes.statement: Narrow-waveform interneurons have a trough-to-peak latency below 0.425 ms, and among wide-waveform units the excitatory cells have a burst index above the threshold separating them from wide-waveform interneurons.
outcomes.source: Figure 1A; STAR Methods, Unit classification
outcomes.quote: Units with trough-to-peak latency < 0.425 ms were classified as narrow-waveform putative interneurons ... Wide-waveform units were grouped into putative excitatory cells (E cells, red; burst index>1.8) and wide-waveform putative interneurons
outcomes.notes: Under both thresholds 98.5% of the 1086 GC and MC are at or above 0.425 ms with a burst index above the threshold, and 90.6% (1.2) or 92.6% (1.8) of the 256 dentate wide-waveform interneurons with a waveform are at or above 0.425 ms with a burst index at or below it. Of 247 dentate narrow-waveform interneurons, 222 (89.9%) are below 0.425 ms, just short of 90%. Two of three groups meet the criterion. CA3 interneurons, judged on their own 0.525 ms threshold, are shown apart (93.8% of narrow ones below it). For 668 units the peak of the waveform falls at the end of the stored 1.6 ms, so their latency is a lower bound. The files do not say whether the stored waveforms (the lab's .spk files) were filtered, while the paper measures "the unfiltered waveform"; whether the criterion should use the unfiltered wide band is asked of a reader (questions/senzai-2017.yaml). No variant with the wide-band waveform meets the criterion in all three groups. In the 17 wide-band files the unfiltered mean over -1 to +2 ms puts 0.744 of narrow-waveform units below 0.425 ms with the latency to the largest later sample, or 0.949 to the first local peak, but then 0.848 of GC and MC and 0.868 of wide-waveform interneurons pass. The stored waveforms of the same 17 files do meet it in all three groups (0.936 of 78 narrow-waveform units, 0.987 of 376 GC and MC, 0.906 (1.2) or 0.915 (1.8) of 106 wide-waveform units), so the shortfall to 0.899 on all files depends on which units are included as well as on the waveform source.
deviations: The groups are the dentate units, as the 0.425 ms threshold is the dentate one (Methods, "CA3 region units were also classified in a similar way into n-I cells (TP latency < 0.525ms)").
The channel of largest amplitude is taken by peak-to-peak amplitude, a standard choice; damaged stored waveforms are left out of the mean.

outcomes.statement: Narrow-waveform interneurons fire faster than wide-waveform interneurons (medians 7.97 and 2.11 Hz; Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.00001).
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The mean firing rates of narrow (median = 7.97 Hz) and wide-waveform (median = 2.11 Hz) interneurons were significantly different
outcomes.notes: Among the 248 narrow-waveform and 258 wide-waveform dentate interneurons, the median rate over the recording span (reading a) is 7.65 and 2.05 Hz, both within tolerance, Kruskal-Wallis P = 1.4e-13. In awake periods (reading b) the medians are 9.23 and 2.87 Hz, outside tolerance. With the CA3 interneurons included the narrow-waveform median is 5.80 Hz (span) or 7.79 Hz (awake).
deviations: The interneurons are the dentate ones, as the paper's counts are ("narrow-waveform (n = 248) and wide-waveform (n = 268) putative interneurons ... Units recorded in CA3 were separately classified", Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1); all labelled interneurons are shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: The waveform of granule cells is narrower than that of mossy cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 3; Figure 1E
outcomes.quote: Overall, the waveform of granule cells was narrower
outcomes.notes: Trough-to-peak latency from the stored waveforms has a median of 0.710 ms for 583 GC and 0.740 ms for 503 MC, Mann-Whitney P = 3.6e-14. The peak falls at the end of the stored 1.6 ms for 44% of GC and 69% of MC, so many latencies are lower bounds. With the unfiltered wide-band waveform at the unit's site (17 files, 136 GC and 240 MC, -1 to +2 ms), the result depends on where the peak is taken. To the largest later sample the medians are 0.770 and 0.800 ms, P = 0.175; to the first local peak, 0.610 and 0.700 ms, P = 7.9e-10. The 300 Hz high-passed wide band gives P = 0.716 and P = 5.2e-10, and the stored waveforms of the same units P = 6.1e-5. The first run's wide-band variant (0.700 against 0.710 ms, P = 0.43) used the high-passed signal over -1 to +1 ms. Whether the criterion should use the unfiltered wide band is asked of a reader.

outcomes.statement: In DRD2-Cre::Ai35 mice, 29 of 107 putative mossy cells were suppressed by green light, against none of 202 putative granule cells, 8 of 68 wide-waveform and none of 69 narrow-waveform interneurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Optogenetic validation of the physiology-based separation of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 1H; STAR Methods, Optogenetic tagging
outcomes.quote: 29 out of 107 putative mossy cells were light responsive ... whereas only eight of 68 w-I interneurons and none of the putative granule cells (n = 202) or n-I interneurons (n = 69) were suppressed significantly by green light
outcomes.notes: In 26 DRD2-Cre::Ai35 files with 20 ms pulses (median 96542 pulses per file), a 20% or larger decrease at +2 to +15 ms against the 20 ms before each pulse is found in 68 of 106 MC (0.642), 6 of 198 GC (0.030), 15 of 62 dentate wide-waveform and 4 of 68 narrow-waveform interneurons. Against 50 to 200 ms after onset, 71 of 106 MC (0.670) and 13 of 198 GC (0.066). The GC fraction is below 0.05 and the MC fraction more than four times it, but the MC fraction is far above 0.271. The unit counts are close to the paper's (107 MC, 202 GC, 68 w-I, 69 n-I). The files' drd2_tagged column marks 29 MC, as the paper, and all 29 are among the MC suppressed here (median response over baseline 0.57, against 0.79 for untagged MC). A significance test added to the 20% decrease (one-sided binomial test of the response count against the baseline count) leaves 68 of 106 MC at P < 0.05 and 65 at P < 0.001, and the pre-pulse rate is not inflated (median 1.07 times the MC rate over the recording). Read per bin, as the Methods' "decreased by >= 20% of the baseline PETH in +2 to +15ms bins" also allows (every 1 ms bin at +2 to +15 ms at least 20% below baseline i), 28 of 106 MC (0.264, within tolerance), 0 of 198 GC, 7 of 62 wide- and 0 of 68 narrow-waveform interneurons are suppressed (paper 29 of 107, 0 of 202, 8 of 68, 0 of 69), and 28 of the 29 tagged MC are among them. The criterion fixes the mean rate over the window, so the outcome is the one tested on it; whether the claims file misreads the Methods is asked of a reader (questions/senzai-2017.yaml), and under the per-bin reading the claim would be reproduced. At light onset the +1 ms bin falls to 0.27 of baseline for GC (pooled over units), 0.25 for MC, 0.39 for n-I and 0.27 for w-I, but the +2 ms bin, the first of the window, is at 0.97 for GC and 1.00 for n-I, which the light does not suppress, so the loss of spikes at onset does not reach into the window.
deviations: The 20% decrease is of the mean rate over +2 to +15 ms, as the claim's criterion has it; a significance test and the per-bin reading of the Methods' passage are variants.
Interneurons are the dentate ones, as for interneuron-rates.

outcomes.statement: Mossy cells are more active than granule cells during both waking and NREM sleep (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for each).
outcomes.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 2A
outcomes.quote: Mossy cells were more active than granule cells during both waking and NREM sleep
outcomes.notes: Median rates in awake periods are 0.726 Hz for MC and 0.079 Hz for GC (Kruskal-Wallis P = 4e-102; with quiet periods added P = 3e-100), and in NREM 0.907 and 0.398 Hz (P = 1e-23). By mouse, the MC median is higher in wake in 13 of the 14 mice with both types, but in NREM in 8 of 14 (in YutaMouse20, 38, 44, 45, 51 and 55 the GC median is higher).

outcomes.statement: Granule cells fire most during NREM sleep and at similar rates during wake and REM.
outcomes.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 2A
outcomes.quote: Granule cells had their highest firing rates during NREM sleep and similar rates during wake and REM
outcomes.notes: GC medians are 0.398 Hz in NREM, 0.079 in wake (awake) and 0.205 in REM (583 units); Kruskal-Wallis P printed as 0, and NREM exceeds wake and REM with Bonferroni-adjusted P printed as 0. Wake and REM also differ (adjusted P printed as 0), so the "similar rates during wake and REM" part does not hold, under both readings of wake (awake+quiet median 0.083 Hz). REM exceeds wake in every mouse.

outcomes.statement: CA3 pyramidal neurons are most active during wake and least active during REM.
outcomes.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 2A
outcomes.quote: CA3 pyramidal neurons were most active during wake and least active during REM
outcomes.notes: CA3 pyramidal cell medians are 0.450 Hz in wake (awake), 0.473 in NREM and 0.305 in REM (568 units). REM is the lowest (adjusted P printed as 0 against both), but wake is not the highest, and wake does not differ from NREM (adjusted P = 0.77; 0.69 with quiet periods, wake median 0.445). By mouse, wake is the highest in 3 of 6 (YutaMouse41, 42, 55).

outcomes.statement: Granule cells increase their firing in NREM sleep compared with waking, while mossy cells fire at equivalent rates in the two states.
outcomes.source: Figure 1D; Discussion, first paragraph
outcomes.quote: Granule cells had cell bodies located near the depth of DS2 reversal, had increased firing in NREM compared to waking ... In contrast, mossy cells ... had equivalent firing rates in NREM and waking
outcomes.notes: The median NREM to wake rate ratio is 4.67 for 583 GC and 1.09 for 503 MC (wake as awake), Mann-Whitney P = 1e-130; with quiet periods 4.31 and 1.10. The GC median ratio is above 2.7 in every mouse. MC NREM and wake rates do differ by a Wilcoxon test (P = 0.0002; with quiet periods P = 4e-6), though the MC median ratio is near 1, so the statement's "equivalent rates" for MC does not hold by that test; the criterion tests the GC half only.

outcomes.statement: Granule cells are more strongly phase-modulated by theta oscillations than mossy cells and fire at later theta phases (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for both).
outcomes.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 2C
outcomes.quote: Granule cells fired on earlier phases of gamma waves ... and later phases of theta oscillations ... Granule cells were more strongly phase-modulated by both gamma ... and theta
outcomes.notes: Of the units with theta phases (566 GC, 501 MC), 464 GC and 470 MC pass Rayleigh P < 0.05 and kappa > 0.1. Their median MRL is 0.429 for GC and 0.347 for MC, Kruskal-Wallis P = 7e-16. GC fire later (circular mean 0.536 rad against 0.246; under reading a, (-pi, pi], medians 0.508 and 0.201, P = 8e-13). Under reading b, [0, 2 pi), the medians are 0.828 and 0.719 and P = 0.59, as the phases lie near 0; that reading splits the cluster of phases and is not a meaningful test. A circular permutation test of the difference of the circular means (10000 shuffles) gives P = 0.0001, the smallest possible, under all five seeds. The GC MRL median is higher in 12 of the 13 mice with both types.
deviations: Phases are from the file's hilus_reference channel, which the files describe as the channel the lab used for theta and gamma phase (its DS2 is positive, as at a hilar site, in all 91 files with a DS2 profile); up to one hour of awake time per file (the median file used the full hour).

outcomes.statement: Granule cells are more strongly phase-modulated by gamma oscillations than mossy cells and fire at earlier gamma phases (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for both).
outcomes.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 2B
outcomes.quote: Granule cells fired on earlier phases of gamma waves ... Granule cells were more strongly phase-modulated by both gamma
outcomes.notes: Of the units with gamma phases (566 GC, 499 MC), 327 GC and 419 MC pass the Rayleigh and kappa test. Median MRL is 0.323 for GC and 0.217 for MC, Kruskal-Wallis P = 3e-34. GC fire earlier (circular mean -0.470 rad against -0.062; reading a medians -0.504 and -0.190, P = 2e-23); under reading b P = 0.67. The circular permutation test gives P = 0.0001 under all five seeds.
deviations: As for theta-modulation.

outcomes.statement: Slow-firing neurons are more strongly coupled to gamma than fast-firing ones (GC r = -0.176, MC r = -0.184, P < 0.0001 for each).
outcomes.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Interestingly, slow firing neurons had stronger phase coupling to gamma waves than fast firing cells
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), all units with a gamma MRL, gives GC r = -0.234 (566 units, P = 2e-8) and MC r = -0.119 (499 units, P = 0.0076); reading (b), units passing the Rayleigh and kappa test, GC r = -0.413 (327, P = 7e-15) and MC r = -0.182 (419, P = 0.00019). Both correlations are negative under both readings, but no reading puts both within tolerance, and the MC P is above 0.0001 under both, so neither the full nor the partial criterion holds. The MC r of reading (b) is within tolerance of -0.184. MRL is biased upward at low spike counts (median 58 gamma spikes per GC, 447 per MC). With every unit with at least 50 spikes (308 GC, 453 MC) subsampled to 50, the correlations mostly vanish, GC r from -0.027 to -0.112 (P 0.05 to 0.64) and MC r from -0.043 to +0.023 (P 0.36 to 0.63) over the five seeds, against -0.129 and -0.064 for the same units with all their spikes.

outcomes.statement: Granule cells are more effectively recruited by type 2 dentate spikes than mossy cells and fire earlier (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for both).
outcomes.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 2D and 2E
outcomes.quote: Granule cells were also more effectively recruited to LFP DS2 than mossy cells ... and fired earlier
outcomes.notes: The median peak ratio around DS2 is 6.70 for 573 GC and 5.04 for 489 MC, Kruskal-Wallis P = 1.9e-6; the median peak time is -3 ms for GC and +1 ms for MC, P = 3e-8. With the DS2 times shifted by 0.5 s the ratios are 1.69 and 1.63. 24 units with no spikes in the baseline window are left out.

outcomes.statement: 5.5% of granule cells monosynaptically excite mossy cells (32 pairs), whereas no mossy cell significantly excites a granule cell.
outcomes.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 1; Figure 3B and 3C
outcomes.quote: The spike transmission probability between excitatory neuron pairs determined that 5.5% of the granule cells monosynaptically excited mossy cells (n = 32 pairs), whereas no mossy cell significantly excited putative granule cells
outcomes.notes: Of 4425 GC-MC pairs recorded together, the Methods' automatic test finds 63 GC to MC pairs and 8 MC to GC pairs. The fraction is 63/583 = 0.108 (reading a), 47/583 = 0.081 (reading b) or 63/4425 = 0.014 (reading c), none within 0.055 +- 0.0055, and MC to GC pairs are found; GC to MC pairs outnumber them 63 to 8. The authors' monosynaptic table in the files holds exactly 32 excitatory GC to MC pairs and no MC to GC pair, as the paper reports (32/583 = 0.055), and the automatic test finds all 32, so the difference is the paper's manual inspection, not repeated here. 34 of the 63 pairs are on one shank.
deviations: The paper's manual inspection of detected pairs is not repeated (criterion); its effect is shown by the authors' table.
The CCG spans +-50 ms and the Gaussian baseline is reflected at its ends, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Spike transmission probability from granule cells to mossy cells increases from the first to the second spike of a granule cell burst (P < 0.001).
outcomes.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 2; Figure 3E to 3G
outcomes.quote: Spike transmission probability increased from first to second spike
outcomes.notes: Over the 63 detected GC to MC pairs, the median transmission probability is 0.0067 for the first burst spike and 0.032 for the second; the second is higher in 56 pairs, paired Wilcoxon P = 2.9e-9. On the authors' 32 pairs, 0.0083 and 0.051, higher in 32 of 32, P = 4.7e-10.

outcomes.statement: GC to MC spike transmission is lower during NREM sleep than during waking (n = 31, P < 0.005).
outcomes.source: Results, State-dependent changes in spike transmission probabilities, paragraph 1; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: Granule cell to mossy cell and granule cell to interneuron comparisons showed reduced probability of spike transmission during NREM compared to wake
outcomes.notes: Over the 63 detected pairs the median transmission probability is 0.0125 in wake and 0.0111 in NREM; NREM is lower in 32 of 63, paired Wilcoxon P = 0.52. On the authors' 32 pairs (the paper's n is 31) the medians are 0.0191 and 0.0129, NREM lower in 19, P = 0.018, which would meet the partial level (P < 0.05) but not P < 0.005. The difference between the two sets is the 31 pairs the paper's manual inspection removed; on those 31 NREM is lower in 13, P = 0.087. The per-pair table is in the notebook.
deviations: Tested on the pairs the automatic test finds (criterion); the authors' curated pairs are a variant.

outcomes.statement: Synchronous co-activation within 1 ms is found in 23% of mossy cells and 9% of CA3 pyramidal cells, but in fewer than 0.2% of granule cell pairs.
outcomes.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Only <0.2% of granule cell pairs showed significant peaks at < 1 ms while 23% of mossy cells and 9% of CA3 pyramidal cells showed synchronous (< 1 ms) co-activation
outcomes.notes: GC pairs are synchronous in 4 of 3105 (0.0013), within the claim's bound of 0.0022. MC and CA3 are synchronous in 0.082 and 0.011 of pairs (reading a) and 216 of 503 MC (0.429) and 46 of 568 CA3 (0.081) have a synchronous partner (reading b); none is within tolerance (CA3 0.0810 falls just outside 0.081 to 0.099). Under reading (b) both exceed the GC pair fraction more than ten times; under (a) CA3 does not (8 times). No pair on one shank is synchronous by the test; over pairs on different shanks MC 0.133 and CA3 0.029. The authors' zero-lag table gives 111 of 503 MC (0.221) and 30 of 568 CA3 (0.053) with a same-type partner, and no GC pair. The criterion says the files do not give each unit's shank; they do, for every file (the units' shank column), so the same-shank and different-shank pairs are shown, and with different shanks only the outcome is the same.
deviations: The paper's manual inspection is not repeated.

outcomes.statement: On the circular T-maze, the fraction of active neurons (above 1 Hz) is higher in the central arm than in the side arms, for granule cells, mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.00001 for each).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: The fraction of active neurons (> 1 Hz) was significantly higher in the central arm compared to the side arms
outcomes.notes: In 33 files with at least 4 light-free runs, the median fraction of units above 1 Hz is 0.328 in central-arm bins and 0.239 in side-arm bins for MC (238 units, Kruskal-Wallis P = 5e-10), 0.018 and 0.022 for GC (225 units, P = 0.41) and 0.233 and 0.219 for CA3 (253 units, P = 0.21). The claim holds at P < 0.00001 for MC only. The run's start is assumed (see the deviations). Under three variants on the run (from the lab's arm_start; without the side-arm samples on the arm not reached; each side-arm sample on the arm its angle gives) MC pass (P from 3e-14 to 5e-8), the GC central median is never above the side one (0.018 against 0.018 to 0.022) and CA3 reach P = 0.05 to 0.67, so each gives the same outcome. Of 1246 light-free runs, 548 hold side-arm samples on the arm not reached, 100 of them more than 10 cm into it; these are 0.386 of all side-arm samples, as a few long runs wander, but the median run has none.
deviations: Assumed that a run starts at the mouse's last entry into the central arm before the lab's arm_start, which lies about 27 cm into the arm, and ends within 10 cm of the reward port (claims file header). The Methods start at the gate opening ("from the gate opening to the arrival to the reward location"), which the files do not mark, and the entry into the arm is the nearest marked point; asked of the authors. Runs from arm_start are a variant.

Side-arm samples are placed on the trial's arm (left_run), so an excursion into the arm not chosen is binned on the chosen one (verifier, round 2); dropping those samples, or placing each on the arm its side_arm_angle gives, are variants.
Units are pooled across sessions and the fraction is taken per bin over the units with a value in it.

outcomes.statement: Few granule cells have two or more place fields on the T-maze (6.6%), against 57.8% of mossy cells and 36.1% of CA3 pyramidal cells (Kolmogorov-Smirnov P < 0.0001).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5C and 5D
outcomes.quote: only a small fraction (6.6% of recorded cells) had two or more. In contrast, 57.8% of mossy cells and 36.1% of CA3 pyramidal neurons had two or more place fields
outcomes.notes: Two or more fields are found in 11 of 225 GC (0.049), 149 of 238 MC (0.626) and 123 of 253 CA3 (0.486) (reading a); of units with a field, 0.275, 0.819 and 0.741 (reading b). Only the MC fraction is within tolerance under reading (a). GC have the lowest fraction, and the GC against MC Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on field counts gives P = 2e-37. Under the three variants on the run (see tmaze-central-active) the fractions are GC 0.031 to 0.040, MC 0.609 to 0.630 and CA3 0.474 to 0.486, KS P 2e-37 to 3e-42, the same outcome.
deviations: Assumed that fields are found from the highest local maximum down (the highest remaining bin, its region above 50% of it, then the next), as the Methods' "50% of the local maximum firing rate" does not say how local maxima are found; asked of the authors.
Runs as in tmaze-central-active (assumed).

outcomes.statement: Granule cells have the lowest within-field peak firing rates (GC against MC, Kolmogorov-Smirnov P < 0.003) and the lowest spatial information of the three types (P < 0.0005).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5E and 5F
outcomes.quote: Of the three neuron types, granule cells had the lowest within-place field peak firing rates ... and lowest spatial information

statistics.about: within-field peak rate, GC against MC

outcomes.notes: The median within-field peak rate is 2.54 Hz for 40 GC with a field and 4.89 Hz for 182 MC (KS P = 0.0005; 3.78 Hz for CA3). The median spatial information is 0.033 bits/s for GC, 0.424 for MC and 0.240 for CA3, KS P = 2e-41 (GC against MC) and 2e-28 (GC against CA3). Under the three variants on the run (see tmaze-central-active) the GC median peak is 1.96 to 3.14 Hz against 4.97 to 5.99 Hz for MC (KS P 0.0002 to 0.0007), and the GC information 0.034 to 0.036 bits/s against 0.448 to 0.529 for MC and 0.246 to 0.256 for CA3 (KS P at most 3e-25), the same outcome.
deviations: Runs (assumed) and fields as in tmaze-multiple-fields; the peak is each unit's highest field peak.

outcomes.statement: The fraction of splitter cells, whose central-arm firing predicts the coming turn, is comparable in granule cells, mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The fraction of splitter cells was comparable in the three principal cell groups
outcomes.notes: Splitters (choice P < 0.001) are 0 of 17 GC, 5 of 158 MC and 3 of 127 CA3 units with a central-arm field, chi-square P = 0.72; over all units (225, 238, 253) P = 0.098. Neither reading finds a difference at P < 0.05. The expected counts are below 1 for GC with a central-arm field (smallest 0.45); an exact (Freeman-Halton) test gives P = 0.835, and 0.096 over all units. One field fit of 901 failed or was degenerate and no unit with a central-arm field lost its test (the first run's helper kept a NaN P when a unit's first field gave one; this is fixed). Splitters are few (8), and with no GC splitter the comparison has little power. Under the three variants on the run (see tmaze-central-active) the splitters are again 0, 5 and 3; from the lab's arm_start of 15, 147 and 108 units with a central-arm field (chi-square P = 0.75), and in the other two variants the counts and P values are unchanged.
deviations: The denominator of the fraction is not given; units with a central-arm field (the units the Methods test) and all units were both run and agree.
Runs as in tmaze-central-active (assumed).

outcomes.statement: For neurons with stable place fields, the remapping index between open fields A and B is above zero in each group (Wilcoxon signed-rank; GC P < 0.05, MC and CA3 P < 0.00001).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 6C and 6D
outcomes.quote: For neurons with significant place fields ... the remapping index was significantly higher than zero in each group
outcomes.notes: Place cells (24 GC, 102 MC, 141 CA3) have median remapping indices of 0.161 (Wilcoxon P = 0.0025), 0.281 (P = 3e-10) and 0.233 (P = 1e-14), each at the paper's level. The open-field files hold 246 GC, 182 MC and 317 CA3 units (paper 247, 181, 317).
deviations: Open fields A, B and A' are the lab's Old, New and Oldlast sessions.

outcomes.statement: Granule cells with stable place fields remap less than mossy cells (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.034; post hoc GC against MC P = 0.028).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 6D
outcomes.quote: but granule cells showed less remapping compared to mossy cells
outcomes.notes: The GC median index (0.161) is below the MC median (0.281; CA3 0.233), but the Kruskal-Wallis test across the three types gives P = 0.69 and the Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney GC against MC P = 1.

outcomes.statement: Only 36.7% of granule cells with place fields (11 of 30) remap, against 61.3% of mossy cells (68 of 111) and 55.6% of CA3 pyramidal cells (80 of 144).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 6C
outcomes.quote: only a minority of granule cells (36.7%, n = 11 out of n = 30 place cells) showed remapping, whereas the majority of both mossy cells (61.3%, n=68 out of n = 111 place cells) and CA3 pyramidal neurons (55.6%, n = 80 out of n = 144) did
outcomes.notes: 11 of 24 GC (0.458), 56 of 102 MC (0.549) and 77 of 141 CA3 (0.546) place cells have an index of at least 0.2. Only the CA3 fraction is within tolerance (MC lies 0.003 below its bound); GC have the lowest fraction. The place-cell counts are 24, 102 and 141 against the paper's 30, 111 and 144.

outcomes.statement: Population-vector remapping is smaller for granule cells than for mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells, for populations of 5, 10, 15 and 20 place cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 3; Figure 6E to 6G
outcomes.quote: The magnitude of population remapping was significantly smaller for granule cells compared to mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells ... These results remained robust within a range of threshold values with different numbers of neurons comprising the population vector
outcomes.notes: Under the claim's seed, the GC median population-vector remapping index is below the MC and CA3 medians at every size, with Kruskal-Wallis P from 2e-11 (n = 5) to 2e-47 (n = 20). At n = 5, 10 and 15 the gap to MC is 0.03 to 0.05; at n = 20 the medians are GC 0.2877, MC 0.2902 and CA3 0.3461, and the Bonferroni GC against MC test gives P = 0.84. Over the five seeds the n = 20 GC median ranges from 0.2858 to 0.2914 and the MC one from 0.2872 to 0.2959; under seeds +2000 (0.2874 against 0.2872) and +4000 (0.2903 against 0.2888) the GC median is above the MC one, so the outcome at n = 20 depends on the draws. The P values are over the 1000 draws, as in the paper (Methods, "Random sampling was performed 1000 times"), and shrink as draws are added. The probability that a GC draw is below an MC draw, which does not, is 0.565 to 0.599 at n = 5 and 0.514 to 0.537 at n = 20 over the five seeds (0.5 is no difference); against CA3 it is 0.546 to 0.579 and 0.682 to 0.713. The GC draws come from 24 place cells. The claim's statistics also list a Bonferroni post hoc test, P < 0.00001 at n = 20 and P < 0.05 at every size, which the criterion leaves out. The post hoc GC against MC test holds at n = 5, 10 and 15 (P at most 1e-6) but not at n = 20 (P = 0.84), so that part of the statement does not hold at n = 20; whether the criterion should include it is asked of a reader (questions/senzai-2017.yaml).
deviations: Draws are from place cells pooled across sessions, without replacement within a draw; pixels count where every drawn cell's maps are defined.

outcomes.statement: Mossy cells rarely inherit place fields from single presynaptic granule cells; of 10 place fields of connected granule cells, only 2 overlapped a field of the postsynaptic mossy cell.
outcomes.source: Results, Transmission of place information between granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 7A and 7B
outcomes.quote: Across 10 place fields from granule cells and 48 place fields from mossy cells, only two place fields showed overlap between monosynaptically connected pairs
outcomes.notes: 28 detected GC to MC pairs are in T-maze files; their GC have 19 fields, of which 5 overlap a field of the partner MC (0.263, within a third). On the authors' pairs, 18 are in T-maze files, as the paper's 18 (Figure 7A), and 3 of their 14 GC fields overlap.
deviations: Fields and runs as in tmaze-multiple-fields (assumed); the variants on the run were not run for this claim.

outcomes.statement: In the open fields, the rate maps of connected granule cells and mossy cells are not correlated within the granule cell's place field (median near 0, n = 19, Wilcoxon P = 0.60).
outcomes.source: Results, Transmission of place information between granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 7J
outcomes.quote: GC-MC map correlations of all comparisons in which the presynaptic GC had significant place fields. Note median correlation around 0
outcomes.notes: Over 18 comparisons (detected pairs, open-field sessions where the GC has a field) the median correlation of the GC and MC maps within the GC field is -0.005, Wilcoxon P = 0.25. On the authors' pairs, 14 comparisons, median -0.117, P = 0.90.

outcomes.statement: Mossy cells are located deeper than granule cells relative to the reversal of the type 2 dentate spike (DS2) (Mann-Whitney P < 0.001).
outcomes.source: Figure 1G; Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: MC were located significantly deeper than GC
outcomes.notes: At the wide-band site, in the 17 files with the wide-band signal, the median DS2 amplitude is 1144 uV for 240 MC and 451 uV for 136 GC, Mann-Whitney P = 5e-44; all MC sites and 82% of GC sites have a positive DS2. The MC median is higher in each of the 15 files with both types but one (YutaMouse33-150223, 1104 against 1187 uV). The stored-waveform site, on all files, gives 1130 and 401 uV, P = 9e-114.
deviations: The DS2 amplitude is the LFP at the DS2 peak minus its mean at -36 to -16 ms (the baseline of the Methods' DS2 detection), averaged over up to 600 DS2 events per file.
The wide-band site uses up to four 52 s blocks of the wide band per file (median 94 spikes per unit).

outcomes.statement: K-means clustering on the DS2 amplitude at the unit's site, the NREM to wake rate ratio and two principal components of the waveform's second derivative separates excitatory dentate units into granule cells and mossy cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 2; Figure 1D to 1F; STAR Methods, Unit classification
outcomes.quote: Based on the bimodality of the distribution, K-means clustering over the four parameters was performed to classify E units into putative GC (yellow) and MC (magenta)
outcomes.notes: K-means on the four standardised features of 376 units (136 GC, 240 MC), with the unfiltered wide-band waveform at the site as the criterion asks, agrees with the labels for 94.4%, under all five seeds. Without the waveform components 89.9%, so the waveform term carries the agreement over 90%; the DS2 amplitude alone 85.1%, the waveform components alone 85.4%, the rate ratio alone 68.9%. With the 300 Hz high-passed wide-band waveform (the first run's main result) 94.9%. The variant with the stored waveforms (first 0.4 ms after the trough, as the stored 1.6 ms often ends sooner) and the table site on all files gives 92.7% of 1086 units.

outcomes.statement: Granule cells reside 59 +- 35 um above the mossy cells they drive.
outcomes.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 1; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: Granule cells resided 59±35 μm above their driven mossy cell partners
outcomes.notes: The distance needs the vertical position of each recording site. The electrodes table holds channel_id, group_name, location, hilus_reference and shank_electrode_number (a channel's place in its shank's list in the lab's .xml file) and no coordinate, and the files do not say which list position is which depth. The probe description names 8 shanks of 8 sites 20 um apart; six mice's shanks hold 10 sites and YutaMouse33's probe has 10 shanks, and the paper's Methods give 20 um vertical separation for both the 8-site (Buzsaki64) and the 10-site (Buzsaki64sp) shanks. On the 261 shanks where the DS2 reverses, its amplitude rises with the list place on some (Spearman above 0.8 on 0.46) and falls on others (below 0 on 0.43), and the sign changes between days of one mouse (YutaMouse42 median 0.39 on 2 November, -0.83 on 13 November). That test cannot tell a list out of depth order from a shank that runs from the hilus into the infrapyramidal blade, where the DS2 reverses again. A smoothness test added in round 2 can. The DS2 profile in list order is smoother than under random orders (P < 0.05) on 0.83 of the 261 shanks under all five seeds, against 0.05 by chance and 0.26 to 0.28 for the order of the LFP columns, on 0.92 of shanks with a positive correlation and 0.71 of those with a negative one. So the lists are in depth order on most shanks, and the site depth can be read from the list place with the lab's convention (first place at the top) and the 20 um spacing; the metadata do not block the claim. The test shows order only, not direction. The example shank fits the convention, and the reading of the negative correlations as shanks reaching the infrapyramidal blade was not tested. Read as depth from the top at 20 um per place, the MC site lies 13 +- 49 um below its GC partner's on the authors' 17 same-shank pairs, and 7 +- 59 um on the 34 of the automatic test (paper 59 +- 35 um). This figure is descriptive only and not a test of the claim, as it places each unit at the electrodes-table site, not the wide-band site used for mc-deeper, and applies one direction to every shank. The claims file gives no criterion for the claim, so it cannot be judged, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified (proposed in round 2, agreed in round 3). The missing criterion is asked of a reader.

outcomes.statement: Granule cell spikes show a delay from the soma to the proximal dendrites, absent in mossy cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 3; Figure S3D to S3F
outcomes.quote: Indeed, the spikes of granule cells showed a delay from the soma to the proximal dendrites ... whereas no such delays were observed in putative mossy cells
outcomes.notes: The soma to dendrite delay needs the order of the sites along the shank. The smoothness test of the DS2 profile (see gc-mc-distance) shows the shank lists in depth order, up to direction, on 0.83 of the shanks where the DS2 reverses, so the order can be read from the list place and the metadata do not block the claim. The claim rests on Figure S3D to S3F, and the claims file gives no criterion for it, so it cannot be judged; the delay was not computed here. The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified (proposed in round 2, agreed in round 3). The missing criterion is asked of a reader, who can take the method from the supplement under paper/, which the claims file's header says was not available.

findings.statement: The electrodes table gives no position for the recording sites, only each channel's place in its shank's list in the lab's .xml file, and does not say which place is which depth. The DS2 profile in list order is smoother than under random orders on 0.83 of the 261 shanks where it reverses (0.05 by chance), so the lists are in depth order on most shanks, but their direction is not stated, and the amplitude rises with the list place on some shanks and falls on others (Spearman below 0 on 0.43), which a shank reaching the infrapyramidal blade could explain. The probe description names 8 shanks of 8 sites 20 um apart, but six mice's shanks hold 10 sites and YutaMouse33's probe has 10 shanks; the paper's Methods give the same 20 um vertical separation for the 10-site shanks. A user can read the site depth from the list place with the lab's convention (first place at the top), which the files do not state.

The trials' arm_start is described as the time the mouse entered the central arm, but at that time the lab's central-arm position is 27.3 cm into the 65 cm arm (median over 1246 light-free runs; 10th to 90th percentile 24.6 to 29.2 cm).

The stored spike waveforms span 1.6 ms (32 samples), and for 44% of granule cells and 69% of mossy cells the waveform peak after the trough falls at the end of that window, so trough-to-peak latencies from them are lower bounds. With the wide-band waveform, in the 17 files that hold it, the unfiltered waveform gives GC and MC latencies of 0.770 and 0.800 ms (P = 0.175) to the largest later sample and 0.610 and 0.700 ms (P = 8e-10) to the first local peak, while the stored waveforms give 0.710 against 0.740 ms (P = 4e-14). The files do not say whether the stored waveforms (the lab's .spk files) were filtered; neither the units table's description nor the waveforms' attributes state a filter. One file (YutaMouse33-150218) has no stored waveforms, as its description says.
13 of the 101 files have no monosynaptic_connections table, and the files do not say whether the authors found no pair in those sessions or did not analyse them.

The files agree with the paper's counts. The labels give 583 GC and 503 MC (paper 586 and 500) and 248 dentate narrow-waveform interneurons (paper 248; wide-waveform 258 against 268). The DRD2-Cre::Ai35 files hold 106 MC, 198 GC, 62 wide- and 68 narrow-waveform dentate interneurons (paper 107, 202, 68, 69), and drd2_tagged marks 29 MC, as the paper, all of them suppressed by light in the data. The authors' monosynaptic table holds the paper's 32 GC to MC pairs and no MC to GC pair, 18 of them in T-maze files as in Figure 7A; its zero-lag table gives 22.1% of MC with a same-type partner (paper 23%). The open-field files hold 246 GC, 182 MC and 317 CA3 units (paper 247, 181, 317).

Checks that passed. The seven same-day 'b' files are separate recordings (different spans, no shared spike counts, distinct global_ids), not duplicate files, and no global_id repeats (whether they hold the same neurons is the last finding). The hilus_reference channel has a positive DS2, as at a hilar site, in all 91 files with a DS2 profile, the largest of its shank in 61. The channel of the largest stored waveform, through the electrodes table, is the channel of the largest wide-band spike for 335 of 376 GC and MC (89%), with a median DS2 amplitude difference of 0 uV between the two. Spikes share the clock of the DS2 events (the GC and MC peak ratio falls with DS2 times shifted by 0.5 s in 80 of 81 files; in YutaMouse44-151130, with few GC and MC, it could not be shown), of the positions (spatial information falls from 0.100 and 0.323 to 0.048 and 0.057 bits/s with spikes shifted 60 s, in two T-maze files) and of the light pulses (all 29 tagged MC suppressed at +2 to +15 ms).

The files do not say whether the two files recorded on the same day (the seven 'b' files and their partners) hold the same neurons, which carry different global_ids. In YutaMouse51 on 16 May, 5 of the 9 GC, MC or CA3 units of the 'b' file (0.56) have a same-type unit on the same shank in the other file of the day whose mean waveform correlates above 0.95 with theirs, against none of 9 in a file of another day. In the other six pairs at most 0.38 of the units do. In YutaMouse54 'b' 2 July 0.10 do, against none in another day's file; in YutaMouse56 'b' 15 September 0.10 do, with no unit of another day to compare; in the other four pairs a file of another day matches as often or more often. The data do not settle it. If the same neurons are in both files, a few units are counted twice.

gone.note: In earlier_findings.ipynb no unit's spike times decrease in any of the 101 files (0 of 4216 units), where the overflow had made the second unit's train restart in 24 files.
gone.statement: In 24 files the end index of the first unit in the units table is short by a multiple of 65,536 spikes (k = 1 to 7). The missing spikes open the second unit's spike train, which then restarts at the beginning of the recording, so the second unit's times are not sorted. The first moved spike follows the first unit's last stored spike by 2 ms to 0.5 s. This looks like an integer overflow at conversion; the waveforms follow the same boundaries.

gone.note: The files now give 6 SST-Cre, 5 DRD2-Cre::Ai35, 4 POMC-Cre::Ai35 and 1 wild type (YutaMouse41). One POMC-Cre::Ai35 mouse is YutaMouse57, which the descriptions say is not in the paper, and the dandiset description says the paper's YM21 is not in the dandiset, so the 15 paper mice are the paper's 16 less one SST-Cre mouse.
gone.statement: The genotypes in the files (6 SST-Cre, 5 Drd2-Cre::Ai35, 4 POMC-Cre::Arch, 1 POMC-Cre::Ai35) do not match the paper's 16 mice (7 SST-Cre, 5 DRD2-Cre::Ai35, 3 POMC-Cre::Ai35 and 1 wild type).

gone.note: Both T-maze series are described in all 45 files with them, central_arm_position (about 2 at the entry of the central arm, falling to 0 toward the side arms) and position (normalized maze coordinates, one unit the 32.5 cm radius of the side-arm circle).
gone.statement: The T-maze position series (`twhl_linearized`, `twhl_norm`) are not described. The values show column 0 of `twhl_linearized` runs along the central arm (0 to 2) and column 1 is an angle along the circular side arms, negative for the left arm, which fits the maze in the Methods but is not stated.

gone.note: The brain_states description now gives each label, with awake as the paper's wake and quiet and transit as labels of the lab's scoring that the paper does not define, so quiet is not the paper's wake.
gone.statement: The states table holds `awake`, `quiet`, `nrem`, `rem` and `transit` without a description; the paper names wake, NREM and REM, and whether `quiet` counts as wake is not stated.

gone.note: Every unit now has a region (DG or CA3). In the paper's 15 mice 248 narrow-waveform interneurons are in the dentate gyrus and 209 in CA3, and 258 wide-waveform ones are dentate, against the paper's 248 and 268.
gone.statement: The interneuron labels (narrow-waveform, wide-waveform) do not say whether the unit is in the dentate gyrus or CA3, which the paper separates; only the excitatory label was split by region (granule cell or CA3 pyramidal cell).

gone.note: The 609 GC and 568 MC include YutaMouse57 (26 GC, 65 MC), which the dandiset and subject descriptions now say is not in the paper; without it the labels give 583 and 503. The units with no row in the unit summary (245) are labelled 'not in unit summary', as the cell_type description says.
gone.statement: The dandiset holds 568 mossy cells and 609 granule cells against the paper's 500 and 586, and 237 units labelled `missing` (units of the spike sorting with no row in the authors' unit summary).

gone.note: PulseStim_5V_20ms_LD12 of YutaMouse57-161006 now holds 64800 onsets with no duplicate and no decrease (none in any of the 1485 series), and the light_pulses description says the 24286 repeated onsets are kept once.
gone.statement: The light-pulse series PulseStim_5V_20ms_LD12 of YutaMouse57-161006 holds 89,086 times of which 24,286 are duplicates, and its times decrease once.

gone.note: All 101 units tables have the same columns, with shank and electrode_group; only YutaMouse33-150218 lacks the waveforms column, as it has no stored waveforms.
gone.statement: The units table has two layouts. 18 files (mice 33, 41, 42 and 54) carry an `electrode_group` column naming each unit's shank, one of them without waveforms (YutaMouse33-150218, which the conversion script lists as excluded); the other 83 files do not.

gone.note: In the 17 wide-band files the largest high-passed wide-band spike of 356 GC, MC and CA3 units lies on the unit's shank for all 356 (earlier 45%) and at the table's site of the largest stored waveform for 333 (0.935, earlier 9%; 0.79 to 1.00 by file).
gone.statement: In the 17 files with the wide-band signal and each unit's shank, the electrodes table's assignment of columns to shanks and sites disagrees with the data. The column where a unit's spike is largest in the wide-band signal lies on the shank the units table gives for 45% of units (11% to 79% by file) and is the table's own site for 9%, and the DS2 amplitude along the table's site numbers crosses zero more than once on 43 of 64 shanks where it crosses at all. The wide-band and LFP columns match each other. The units' shanks (`electrode_group`) and stored waveform channels fit the wide-band signal under one fixed map of columns, the same in all 4 mice (a map from three mice gives the column of a unit's largest spike for 78% to 89% of units in the fourth, against 5% to 13% for the table), so the error is in the table, whose blocks of 8 rows do not match the probe's columns.

outcomes.note: Both attempts read the same labels, 609 GC and 568 MC over all 16 mice. Version 0.261122.2143 says in its dandiset and subject descriptions that YutaMouse57 (26 GC, 65 MC) is not in the paper, which version 0.260218.2052 did not, so senzai-2017-02 left it out and counted 583 and 503, both within tolerance, where the earlier MC count of 568 was outside 450 to 550.

The earlier version did not give an interneuron's region, so senzai-2017-01 pooled dentate and CA3 interneurons (medians 5.96 and 2.57 Hz over the span, outside tolerance). The region column of this version lets senzai-2017-02 take the dentate ones, as the paper's counts are, giving 7.65 and 2.053 Hz, both within tolerance; pooled with CA3 its narrow-waveform median is 5.80 Hz. The earlier 17-file variant of dentate shanks had already given 8.56 and 2.29 Hz.

The earlier outcome rests on reading (b), GC r = -0.397 and MC r = -0.253 with P below 0.0001 over all 16 mice; senzai-2017-02 left out YutaMouse57, which this version says is not in the paper, and its MC r is -0.182 with P = 0.00019. A check made for this reconciliation, with senzai-2017-02's phase code on all files, gives its numbers exactly without YutaMouse57 and MC r = -0.245 (472 units, P = 7.1e-08) with it, while the earlier rules (at least 10 spikes, awake periods of 10 s, kappa without correction) change nothing on the 15 mice (MC r = -0.182, P = 0.00019).

disagreements.reason: Taken literally at seed offset 0 the criterion is met for every size, but at n = 20 GC and MC differ by 0.0025 and GC > MC under 2 of 5 seeds (Bonferroni P 0.84 at seed 0); only sizes 5, 10 and 15 hold robustly (cell 64). Point 8, neither the dandiset nor the asset metadata has site coordinates, but the files hold shank_electrode_number, the probe description (8 sites, 20 um vertical steps) and a per-file DS2 profile, which could have confirmed the lab's convention of listing channels by depth, and 34 of the 63 GC to MC pairs are on one shank; metadata_insufficient overstates the case, the real block is that the claims file has no criterion. Same as gc-mc-distance; the multi-channel stored waveforms and the wide-band signal in 17 files could give a site-ordered delay, if the depth order were established.

paper_notes.statement: The Methods define a T-maze place field as a region "above 50% of the local maximum firing rate" but not how local maxima are found when a map has several peaks. This attempt takes the highest remaining bin, its region, then the next; the count of fields per unit, and so tmaze-multiple-fields and inheritance-tmaze, depend on this. How were local maxima found?

For DRD2-Cre::Ai35 mice the Methods identify mossy cells by a decrease of at least 20% "in +2 to +15ms bins", and the Results say "suppressed significantly". A 20% decrease of the mean rate over the window, against either baseline, finds 68 of 106 MC suppressed (paper 29 of 107), and a significance test does not lower this. A 20% decrease in every 1 ms bin against the 20 ms before the pulse finds 28 of 106, and 28 of the 29 MC the files tag. Was the rule applied to each bin, and what baseline window and what significance test were used?

The automatic CCG test of the Methods finds 63 GC to MC and 8 MC to GC pairs; the authors' curated table holds 32 and 0. The manual inspection that "excluded the contamination from the long-time scale trend" changes the fraction (monosyn-gc-to-mc) and the state result (state-transmission, P = 0.52 on the 63 pairs, 0.018 on the 32). What criteria did the inspection apply?

The T-maze analysis window runs "from the gate opening to the arrival to the reward location", but the files mark no gate opening; this attempt starts each run at the mouse's entry into the central arm. Where does the gate opening fall relative to the files' trial times?

The Methods give a burst index threshold of 1.2 for excitatory cells, and the Figure 1A legend gives 1.8. The labels in the files do not show which was used: of the 1654 GC, MC and CA3 units of the paper's 15 mice with a burst index, 12 lie between 1.2 and 1.8, as do 8 of the 320 wide-waveform interneurons.

entries.name: senzai-2017
entries.title: Granule cells and mossy cells of the dentate gyrus (Senzai and Buzsaki 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Senzai and Buzsaki (2017) on dandiset 000003, silicon probe recordings from the dentate gyrus and CA3 of 15 of the paper's mice. It compares granule cells, mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells by the authors' labels, their waveforms, rates by brain state, theta and gamma phase locking, firing around dentate spikes, optogenetic suppression in DRD2-Cre mice, monosynaptic and zero-lag pairs from cross-correlograms, place fields on the circular T-maze and remapping between open fields, and repeats the paper's k-means separation of granule and mossy cells on the files that hold the wide-band signal.
